verses.text: Job, please hear me out and listen to everything I have to say.
I’ve opened my mouth, and I’m ready to speak.
I’ll speak honestly from my heart and tell you sincerely what I know.
The Spirit of God made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me if you can. Get your words in order and take your stand.
I’m just like you before God. I too was shaped from clay.
You have no reason to be afraid of me. I won’t put any heavy pressure on you.
I heard you speak. These are the words I heard you say:
‘I’m clean and haven’t rebelled. I’m innocent, and there’s no wrongdoing in me.
Yet God finds reasons to accuse me. He treats me like his enemy.
He locks my feet in stocks and watches every path I take.’
Here’s my answer. You’re wrong about this, because God is greater than any human.
Why do you argue with him over his refusal to explain what he does?
God speaks once and then again, though people pay no attention.
He speaks in a dream, in a vision at night, when people are in a deep sleep on their beds.
Then he opens their ears and makes sure his warning sinks in.
He wants to turn them away from what they were set on doing and keep them from pride.
He keeps them from going down to the pit and saves their lives from the sword.
A person can also be corrected through pain in bed, with an endless ache in their bones.
They can’t stand the thought of bread. Even their favorite food makes them sick.
They waste away until there’s nothing left of their flesh, and bones that used to be hidden stick out.
Their life comes close to the pit, and they draw near to those who bring death.
But there may be an angel at their side, a messenger one in a thousand, to show them what is right for them.
Then God has mercy and says, ‘Keep them from going down to the pit. I’ve found a ransom.’
Their flesh will be fresher than a child’s, and they’ll regain the strength of their youth.
They pray to God, and he welcomes them. They see his face with joy, and he restores them to a right standing.
They sing in front of others, ‘I sinned and twisted what was right, and I gained nothing from it.
God saved me from going down to the pit. Now I’ll live to see the light.’
God does all this for a person twice and even three times,
to bring them back from the pit so the light of the living can shine on them.
Pay attention, Job, and listen to me. Stay quiet and let me speak.
If you have something to say, answer me. Speak up, because I want to see you cleared.
Otherwise, listen to me. Be quiet, and I’ll teach you wisdom.”
